rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is nonexistent. This experiment tests the effect of multimodal fusion (concat) in a singleprofile setup with PCA and ResNet50 encoders. It clarifies whether combining RNA and image data improves performance, addressing a key design choice (multimodal vs single modality) that could significantly impact results. It isolates the fusion method's effect while keeping other factors minimal, providing foundational insights with high informational value.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with concat fusion (config_016) achieve 0.5266 validation accuracy. This experiment tests whether switching to weighted fusion (config_017) improves performance, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. It directly addresses uncertainty about whether weighted fusion could yield better results than simple concatenation, while keeping other design choices (model_setting, profile_setting, encoders) consistent. This comparison is critical for understanding fusion mechanism impact under limited budget.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with singleprofile, pca_n2000, and resnet50 have similar performance (0.5266 vs 0.5232). This experiment tests the impact of switching the RNA encoder to scvi_n200 (a more complex model) while keeping other parameters identical, isolating the effect of RNA representation. This addresses uncertainty about whether more sophisticated encoders improve performance in this setup.

Existing evidence shows that scvi_n200 (RNA encoder) with singleprofile and multimodal setup (config_028) achieves the highest accuracy (0.536). This experiment tests whether switching to multiprofile while retaining scvi_n200 and resnet50 (same as config_028) improves performance, isolating the effect of profile setting. It balances exploitation of the strong RNA encoder with exploration of multiprofile, a key design choice with uncertain impact.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, and weighted fusion (config_029) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.5399). This experiment tests whether extending to multiprofile settings (a key design choice) with the same encoders and weighted fusion improves performance, while also evaluating the impact of avgpool aggregation. It isolates the effect of profile setting and aggregation, building on the promising direction of scvi_n200 and weighted fusion.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile setups with scvi_n200 RNA encoder and resnet50 image encoder (config_031) achieve high validation accuracy (0.6776). This experiment tests replacing resnet50 with imagenet_vit_l (a more powerful image encoder) while keeping RNA encoder, aggregation (avgpool), and fusion (weighted) consistent. This isolates the effect of the image encoder, which is critical for improving performance. It balances exploitation (building on config_031's success) and exploration (testing a stronger encoder).

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder (config_037) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.706). This experiment tests whether a single modality (RNA-only) with the same scvi_n200 encoder and multiprofile setting (which has shown strong performance in previous multimodal models) can match or exceed this performance. It isolates the impact of modality choice while keeping RNA encoder and aggregation consistent, addressing uncertainty about whether multimodal approaches are strictly necessary.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile settings with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_037) achieve the highest accuracy. This experiment tests replacing scvi_n200 with scgpt RNA encoder while keeping other parameters the same, isolating the effect of RNA encoder choice. It directly compares a promising RNA encoder (scgpt) against the current best (scvi_n200) in the most successful configuration, balancing exploration and exploitation.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_037) achieve the highest accuracy (0.706). This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation while maintaining weighted fusion could further improve performance, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It is the best use of the next experiment as it directly explores a key design choice with potential to enhance performance without overcomplicating the model.

Existing evidence shows that using 'transformer' aggregation and 'weighted' fusion with 'imagenet_vit_l' image encoder (e.g., config_039) achieves high accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder from 'scvi_n200' to 'scgpt' (another advanced encoder) maintains or improves performance under the same aggregation/fusion setup. This isolates the impact of RNA encoder choice, a critical design decision, while leveraging the strong foundation of the top-performing configuration.
